cases.prompt: We defined a use case for a downtime view for shift supervisors. Before we write the business case, I want to know whether supervisors would actually use the screen. Can we do a quick mock-up and test it with them?
cases.expected_output:
The open question is named in the plant's words and classed as usability.
A click-dummy (mock-up) is chosen, not a PoC.
A pass criterion with a number, scope, time box and named validator is written before any build.
The label is mock-up, and the result is never called proven.
A validation record is the output.

cases.prompt: Does the vibration signal on our pump actually separate good from worn bearings? We have two months of readable data. Should we run a proof of concept before going to the business case?
cases.expected_output:
The question is classed as a data or model question, so a PoC on real data is picked.
The data verdict from the data check is confirmed first.
The pass criterion is written before the PoC with a validator role.
The label is PoC and no euro figure is attached.

cases.prompt: Build me a prototype that predicts oven failures. The oven has no logged signals at all, but the plant manager is keen to see something.
cases.expected_output:
The skill stops because a prototype on missing data proves nothing.
The data gap is routed to the data availability check.
At most a click-dummy for a usability question is offered, labelled mock-up.
No invented plant values are presented as real.

cases.prompt: Can you work out how many euros per year the new scrap-tracking use case will save so I can put it in the business case?
cases.expected_output:
It is recognised that this is a value question, which a prototype cannot answer.
The request is pointed to the business case building skill.
No prototype is started.
